@graph.comment: Mints the ID-JAGs (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grants) the storages' authorization servers trade for access tokens. Signed with the Solid-OIDC key, so the existing `/.oidc/jwks` publishes the verification key. See openwiki/architecture/id-jag-access-claims.md.

The access tokens of this OpenID provider are the LWS authentication credentials of its users: the UI and other clients of this server exchange them at the UAS below for ID-JAGs. Restricting them to this server (`aud` = `iss`) keeps them from being replayed at another authorization server; `cnf.jkt` (DPoP) proves possession on top of that. Solid-OIDC deployments keep the default `solid` audience.

Verifies the first-hop authentication credential at this UAS locally: a self-issued `at+jwt` with `iss` = this UAS, `aud` including this UAS, `cnf.jkt` matching the DPoP proof, and a signature made with this UAS's JwkGenerator key. No OIDC discovery, no subject document, no WebID/Solid-OIDC, and no CID suite.

Accepts an incoming ID-JAG at a UAS for the C2 impersonation hop (Bob -> YoYo). The signature/audience/claim are verified before the handler re-issues it under the visible subject. A local issuer skips the subject document; a federated issuer is resolved through the subject CID document's `lws:OpenIdProvider` service.

Read-only admin impersonation (org context): an admin of an organization may have this UAS issue an ID-JAG as that organization for one peer storage. The authority is the organization's DataRegistry-scoped AdminGrant (assignee = the admin, client = the admin's own authorization agent); the claim is derived from the organization's grants and narrowed to odrl:read. Referenced by the token handler's `adminImpersonationAuthority`.
Independent UAS check (C4): an incoming delegated ID-JAG claim must match a grant the assigner issued and stores in their own grant registry before this UAS re-issues it.

LWS token endpoint of the UAS: exchanges the user's DPoP-bound access token (or an incoming ID-JAG at an impersonation hop) for an ID-JAG restricted to one storage's authorization server. A regular ID token is rejected.

handler.comment: Admin impersonation (org context): the requested scope selects read-only impersonation of the organization named by the `impersonate` parameter. The organization's UAS checks its AdminGrant, derives the organization's claim for the requested peer storage, narrows it to odrl:read and issues the ID-JAG as the organization — the admin is dropped from here on. Audiences: storage/UAS base URLs, `.sai` URLs under this UAS, and `.sai` URLs of configured peer UASs (agent discovery uses their base URL).
